To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the economic, security, and democratic accountability variables have no significant impact on military expenditures in NATO countries.
the traditional NATO countries are driven by economic and political factors, while the new member countries are driven by security factors.
the economic determinants are the most significant for traditional NATO countries, the security determinants are the second most important, while the political determinants are the least influential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
a comprehensive analysis of the determinants affecting the military expenditure in selected NATO countries.
the question whether the military expenditures of the NATO countries are determined by economic factors, security factors, political factors, or a combination of these factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the determinants of the military expenditures of the traditional NATO countries are more or less the same as the determinants of those of the new NATO countries, although some differences can be identified.
the economic and political determinants of military spending are more significant for traditional NATO member countries, while security determinants are more important for new NATO member countries.
the economic determinants of military spending in the traditional NATO member countries are much more important than in the new member countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the security and political risks are the most important factors influencing military expenditures in NATO countries.
economic and political determinants of military expenditure are significant and consistent in traditional NATO countries, while security determinants are significant and inconsistent.
the economic determinants of military spending in NATO countries are not very strong and are not significant in all countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
economic and political determinants of military spending are more significant than security determinants.
the economic determinants of military spending in the new NATO members are more important than security and political determinants.
the traditional determinants of military spending are not sufficient to explain the level of military expenditures of the NATO countries.
